document: The team reviewed progress on the document intelligence roadmap. The summarization feature can ingest long meeting notes, articles, and PDF text. Engineering reported that the local extractive summarizer is fast enough for interactive demos. The machine learning roadmap includes fine-tuning BART-large on labeled document-summary pairs and evaluating quality with ROUGE-L. Design proposed a Streamlit interface with a file uploader, summary length control, and summary text area. Product requested summaries under 300 words by default. Action items include finishing the benchmark script, refining the app, and collecting synthetic examples.
summary: The team reviewed a document summarization roadmap covering meeting notes, articles, and PDF text. Engineering will maintain a fast extractive baseline while preparing BART-large fine-tuning and ROUGE-L evaluation. Design will build a Streamlit uploader with summary length controls, and product wants default summaries under 300 words.

document: Document summarization systems help users understand long-form information quickly. Extractive summarizers select important sentences from the original text and are fast, deterministic, and easy to evaluate. Abstractive summarizers generate new wording and can be more fluent, but they require stronger models and validation. A practical portfolio design combines a local extractive baseline with optional fine-tuned transformer support and reports ROUGE-L plus latency.
summary: Document summarizers condense long-form information. Extractive methods are fast and deterministic, while abstractive methods can be more fluent but need stronger validation. A practical project combines a local baseline, optional transformer fine-tuning, ROUGE-L evaluation, and latency reporting.
